items.followUp: State two more properties that make a liquid suitable for use in a thermometer.

rubric.why: The question asks for any two valid properties of a thermometric liquid.
rubric.description: Gives any two distinct suitable properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each valid property, up to 2 marks.

modelAnswer: A thermometric liquid should expand uniformly with temperature.
It should have a low freezing point and a high boiling point.

items.followUp: Derive the second equation of motion using a velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: The displacement is the area under the velocity-time graph.
rubric.description: Writes the trapezium-area expression for displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relation.

rubric.why: This uses the definition of acceleration for uniform acceleration.
rubric.description: Relates acceleration, initial velocity, final velocity and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either equivalent relation.

rubric.why: Substituting the acceleration relation eliminates time from the displacement equation.
rubric.description: Eliminates time and obtains the rearranged displacement relation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct intermediate result.

rubric.why: This is the third equation of motion.
rubric.description: States the third equation of motion correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final equation.

modelAnswer: For a velocity-time graph with initial velocity u and final velocity v, displacement s is the area under the graph.
s = area of trapezium = 1/2 (u + v)t
Acceleration, a = (v − u)/t, so t = (v − u)/a.
Substituting in the displacement equation: s = 1/2 (u + v)(v − u)/a
Therefore, 2as = (u + v)(v − u) = v² − u²
Hence, v² = u² + 2as.

items.followUp: Explain how a hydraulic press multiplies an applied force.

rubric.why: A hydraulic system works by transmitting pressure through an enclosed liquid.
rubric.description: States the principle of equal pressure transmission in an enclosed liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying Pascal's principle or equivalent.

rubric.why: The pressure produced at the small piston is force divided by its area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct input-pressure relation.

rubric.why: Equal pressure at both pistons gives the force-area relationship.
rubric.description: Relates the forces and areas of the two pistons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship.

rubric.why: The larger output piston produces a greater force, so the system acts as a force multiplier.
rubric.description: Explains that the larger piston gives a greater output force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the force-multiplier conclusion.

modelAnswer: A hydraulic system consists of two pistons of areas A₁ and A₂ connected by an enclosed liquid.
By Pascal's principle, pressure applied to the liquid is transmitted equally throughout it.
If force F₁ is applied to the small piston, the pressure is P = F₁/A₁.
The same pressure acts on the large piston, so P = F₂/A₂.
Therefore, F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂, and F₂ = F₁A₂/A₁.
Since A₂ is greater than A₁, F₂ is greater than F₁; hence the hydraulic system multiplies force.

items.followUp: Define velocity and write its formula.

rubric.why: Acceleration describes how quickly velocity changes with time.
rubric.description: Defines acceleration as the rate of change of velocity with time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The formula expresses the change from initial to final velocity per unit time.

modelAnswer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
a = (v − u)/t, where u is initial velocity, v is final velocity and t is time.

items.followUp: Give two examples of how friction is useful in everyday life.

rubric.why: Friction enables everyday actions and controls motion; without it, these actions would fail.
rubric.description: States two valid consequences of friction disappearing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each distinct consequence.

modelAnswer: Without friction, we would not be able to walk because our feet would slip.
Moving objects would continue moving without slowing down, and vehicles could not be stopped by brakes.

items.followUp: Define unstable equilibrium and give one example.

rubric.why: A body in stable equilibrium returns to its original position after a small displacement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.why: The question requires two examples of stable equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when two valid examples are stated.

modelAnswer: A body is in stable equilibrium if, after a small displacement, it tends to return to its original position.
Examples: a ball at the bottom of a bowl, and a book lying on a table.
